title: Eight Billion Souls
body:
Eight billion souls beneath one restless sky,
each carrying a universe no map could find.
I am a speck the stars will never recognise,
and still, a whole world lives behind my eyes.

Somewhere, a stranger is laughing at a kitchen table.
Somewhere, someone is learning how grief sounds.
Somewhere, two people are meeting for the first time,
unaware that the future has just changed shape.

We are so small the cosmos cannot hear us.
We are so vast that a single kindness
can alter the weather of another life.

Perhaps being human is this:
to be almost nothing to the universe,
and everything, briefly, to one another.
line: We are almost nothing, and still we matter to one another.

title: The House With One Light
body:
At the end of a tired street
stands a house with peeling paint
and one light left burning.

The garden has forgotten its flowers.
The gate leans into the wind.
The windows hold the dark
like hands cupped around water.

People pass and call it empty.
They do not see the table set for two,
the book left open,
the small stubborn glow in the hall.

I have been that house.
I have watched other windows brighten
and wondered what was wrong with mine.

Still, every evening,
someone turns the light on.
Not because they know who is coming,
but because they have not yet agreed
that nobody will.
line: Hope can be an action before it becomes a feeling.

title: The Irony of It All
body:
I have a thousand things to tell you
and no sentence that feels safe.
I have people who would answer the phone
and still rehearse my loneliness in silence.

I collect plans like postcards
from countries I have not visited.
I laugh at the right moments.
I say, “I'm good,” with such convincing ease
that sometimes even I believe it.

The irony is not that life is hard.
It is that life keeps offering me beauty
while I am busy looking for proof
that I do not belong here.

Tonight, the kettle sings.
A moth circles the lamp.
Somewhere a dog barks at the moon.
The world continues being strange and generous.

I am trying to notice.
line: Sometimes the world offers beauty before we feel ready to receive it.

title: The People Who Passed Through
body:
Some people leave like doors slamming.
Others leave like summer does—
so gradually you keep dressing for the warmth.

You do not know the last ordinary afternoon
is the last ordinary afternoon.
You do not memorise the sound of their keys,
or the way they say your name
when they are half-asleep.

Later, a song returns them.
A street corner borrows their outline.
You find their kind of laugh
in a stranger across a crowded room.

They were not yours forever.
They were yours for a chapter,
which is a smaller thing than forever
and a larger thing than nothing.

I hope they are well.
I hope I am, too.
line: A chapter can end without becoming meaningless.

title: Three in the Morning
body:
At three in the morning,
the ceiling becomes a cinema
and my mind buys every ticket.

What if I leave?
What if I stay?
What if the life I keep imagining
is waiting behind a door I have walked past?

The clock has no opinion.
The fridge hums its small philosophy.
A car moves through the street
like a thought finally letting go.

I ask the future for a map.
It sends me another question.
I ask the past to explain itself.
It sends me a photograph
where everyone is laughing
and nobody knows what comes next.

At three in the morning,
I do not solve my life.
I learn that morning is still coming
without my permission.
line: Not every question needs an answer before sunrise.

title: The Colour You Never Were
body:
I could have been the prettiest shade of red,
bright enough to stop a room,
soft enough to stay in memory.
But your favourite colour was purple.

So I made a home inside the almost:
almost chosen, almost understood,
almost the person you meant
when you said you wanted someone like me.

For a while I mistook changing
for the same thing as being loved.
I sanded down my edges,
learned the music you preferred,
called the silence compromise.

Then one afternoon I wore my own colours
and nothing terrible happened.
The sky did not split.
The world did not turn away.

You were allowed to want purple.
I was allowed to remain red.
line: Love should not require you to become someone else.

title: An Unsent Letter to the Future
body:
Dear future me,
I hope you remember how uncertain this felt.
How every choice seemed to close a hundred doors,
how the word forever sounded both beautiful
and a little like a locked room.

I hope you have gone somewhere unfamiliar.
I hope you have been brave in small ways:
asked the question, made the call,
left when staying made you smaller.

If you are not where we planned to be,
please do not call us a failure.
Plans are maps drawn by people
who have not yet met all their weather.

Tell me you kept something ordinary sacred.
A slow morning. A good song.
A person who laughs with their whole face.

And if you are still afraid,
I hope you went anyway.
line: The future is not a test you must pass perfectly.

title: The Museum of Almosts
body:
In the first room: the message never sent,
framed in a light too gentle for regret.

In the second: a key to an apartment
that two people once discussed
as if desire were a lease they could sign.

There is a train ticket to a city
we kept promising we would see.
A photograph cropped just before the argument.
A little paper star labelled “someday.”

Visitors move quietly through the exhibits.
Nobody touches anything.
Everyone recognises something.

At the exit, the curator has left a note:
An almost is not a life you failed to live.
It is evidence that you wanted.

Outside, the street is full of doors.
Some of them are open.
line: Wanting something is not proof that you lost it.

title: The Paradox of Wanting to Be Known
body:
Please understand me completely,
but do not look too closely
at the rooms I keep locked.

Ask what hurts.
I will tell you something manageable.
Ask what I want.
I will make it sound like a joke.
Ask if I am afraid.
I will describe the weather.

I want the impossible tenderness
of being seen without being examined,
of being known without becoming
an argument someone can win.

Maybe intimacy is not a person
finding every hidden room.
Maybe it is the moment you open one door
and they do not rush ahead.

They wait on the threshold.
They let you choose the light.
line: Being understood begins with the freedom to be honest slowly.

title: The Things That Make Us Human
body:
We build walls and call them safety.
We build bridges and call them hope.
We invent borders, then cross oceans
for a voice that sounds like home.

We can be cruel with perfect manners,
kind without an audience,
wrong for years and changed in a morning.

We bury our dead with flowers
and our living with expectations.
We make machines that travel to the stars
and still forget to ask the neighbour
if they have eaten.

There is no single answer to us.
Only the daily choice:
what will these hands make possible,
what will this mouth refuse to wound,
who will be less alone because I was here?
line: Our contradictions are real; so is the choice we make next.

title: An Ordinary Morning
body:
The kettle clicks off.
A stripe of sun finds the floor.
The neighbour shakes a rug
as if dust were a small confession.

Nothing has changed.
No grand revelation arrives.
The day does not know it is a day
I might remember years from now.

I stand barefoot in the kitchen
and drink water from a glass.
Outside, a child is learning to whistle.
Somewhere, a person is being missed.

I used to think a meaningful life
would announce itself with music.
Now I suspect it may be quieter:
a morning that asks nothing of me
except that I am here to see it.
line: Not every beautiful thing arrives dramatically.

title: Instructions for Being Young
body:
You will think everyone else received
instructions you somehow missed.
They did not.
They are improvising in nicer clothes.

You will mistake urgency for destiny,
attention for affection,
and a closed door for a verdict
on the whole architecture of your life.

You will change your mind.
Let this be a talent.
You will outgrow rooms
where you once begged to belong.
Let this be a kind of weather.

Take the long way home sometimes.
Learn one thing badly before learning it well.
Love people without making them your future.

You are not late.
You are alive at the beginning
of a story that does not owe anyone
an early explanation.
line: Being unfinished is not the same as being behind.

title: A Small Rebellion
body:
Today I did not turn my rest into guilt.
I let the message wait.
I walked beneath a sky
that had not asked me to be productive.

The world kept spinning.
Nobody came to confiscate my future.
The sun went on making gold
from ordinary windows.

Perhaps rebellion is sometimes
less a revolution in the streets
than a refusal to call yourself lazy
for being a living creature
with a body that needs a pause.

Tomorrow I may run again.
Today I sat on the steps
and watched the light change.
line: Rest can be a quiet form of resistance.

title: The Unfinished Map
body:
I wanted a map with every road marked,
every danger named in a neat red circle,
every ending printed in advance.

Instead I got weather,
a few good shoes,
and people who sometimes knew the way
until the road changed.

I have taken wrong turns
that introduced me to myself.
I have lost years to doors
that were never going to open.
I have arrived late and found
that the important thing was still there.

The map remains unfinished.
So do I.
There is comfort in this:
we are allowed to keep becoming
without apologising for the draft.
line: A life can be meaningful before it is resolved.

title: Coffee for Two
body:
You ordered yours without sugar.
I remembered, which is a small thing
until it is the only thing
that tells you someone has been paying attention.

We talked about traffic,
the strange price of fruit,
a film neither of us had finished.
The afternoon made no promises.
The cups cooled between us.

I think love may begin like this:
not fireworks, not fate,
but a mind making room
for the small facts of another person.

I did not tell you I was happy.
I was afraid the word might startle it.
So I watched you stir your coffee
and let the ordinary become enough.
line: Tenderness often lives in the details we remember.

title: The Last Page
body:
I read the last page twice
as if the story might reconsider.
The characters had become familiar
in the way places become familiar
when you have been lost there long enough.

Outside, the kettle was cold.
The afternoon had moved on without me.
I put the book back on the shelf
with the care of returning someone home.

There are endings that hurt
because they were beautiful,
not because they were wrong.

I opened another book.
Not to replace the first,
but because a life made only of endings
would never learn the shape
of a beginning.
line: An ending can honour what came before it.

title: The Room Inside
body:
There is a room inside me
where every version of myself sits down.
The child with scraped knees.
The teenager who knew everything.
The stranger I became to survive a season.

They do not always agree.
One wants to run.
One wants to be chosen.
One keeps checking the locks.

I used to call this inconsistency.
Now I call it a meeting.
We are trying to decide
what kind of life we can build
without asking any of us to disappear.

Tonight I leave the door ajar.
No one has to speak.
We can simply share the room.
line: Healing may begin when you stop exiling your own selves.

title: A Letter to Time
body:
Dear Time,
I have accused you of stealing
what I was too distracted to hold.
I have asked you to hurry
and begged you to stay.

You make children of strangers
and strangers of old friends.
You turn a house into a memory
before the paint has dried.

Still, I cannot call you only cruel.
You softened some griefs.
You taught my hands new work.
You let the unbearable become
something I can carry to the shops.

I do not understand your rules.
But if you must keep moving,
teach me to arrive where I am
before the moment becomes a story.
line: Presence is one way of meeting time halfway.

title: A Place at the Table
body:
I kept a place for you
long after you stopped coming.
Not a chair, exactly—
more the shape of a possibility
I kept setting down beside me.

I told myself it was patience.
Sometimes it was hope.
Sometimes it was fear dressed neatly
as loyalty.

The table did not judge me.
It held the plates, the crumbs,
the quiet evenings I made a meal of anyway.

One night I put the extra chair away.
The room looked larger.
I felt both cruel and free.

There is a difference between loving someone
and refusing to let your life begin
until they arrive.
line: You can release the waiting without denying the love.

title: The City After Rain
body:
The city after rain looks briefly forgiven.
Neon trembles in the gutters.
The pavement keeps a second sky.

A man closes his umbrella
and shakes the world from its edges.
Two strangers share the shelter
of a shop that has already shut.

Everything smells newly possible,
though nothing has changed its address.
The bus is late.
The news is bad.
The future remains itself.

Still, the street shines.
For a moment the ordinary world
wears its hidden silver lining
without asking anyone to believe in it.
line: Beauty does not require the world to be fixed.

title: The Universe Does Not Answer
body:
I sent a question into the dark
and waited for the stars to rearrange.
They continued burning
with their ancient indifference.

No sign arrived.
No voice explained the timing,
the loss, the strange luck
of meeting you on that particular Tuesday.

At first I called this emptiness.
Then I noticed the freedom inside it:
no cosmic verdict had been issued.
No invisible hand had signed my failure.

The universe did not answer.
The kettle boiled.
My friend called.
A small green shoot split the soil.

Perhaps meaning is not delivered.
Perhaps it is what we make
while the stars keep their distance.
line: Silence from the universe leaves room for human choices.

title: The Quiet Brave
body:
Courage is not always a speech
or a hand raised against a crowd.
Sometimes it is a boundary
said in an ordinary voice.

Sometimes it is beginning again
without announcing the comeback.
Sometimes it is admitting
that the dream has changed shape.

The brave are not always fearless.
They are often tired,
carrying a bag with a broken strap,
walking anyway because the bus has gone.

I hope you count these moments.
The world has enough statues
for people who never trembled.
I want to remember the ones
who did, and moved.
line: Quiet courage still counts.

title: The Photograph
body:
In the photograph, nobody is looking
at the camera at the same time.
Someone is laughing too hard.
Someone is halfway out of frame.
Someone has not yet learned
the name of the grief that will find them.

I used to think a photograph
was proof that happiness had happened.
Now I see it is proof
that a moment agreed to stay still
long enough for us to notice.

We were not as certain as we looked.
We were not as safe as we felt.
But we were there,
under the same light,
being young in a way
we could not yet recognise.
line: Memory preserves the moment, not the whole truth.

title: The Art of Staying
body:
Stay, not because you are afraid to leave,
but because the room has become a place
where both of you can breathe.

Stay through the unphotogenic hours:
the tired face, the misplaced keys,
the conversation that needs a second try.

Stay curious about the person
who keeps changing inside the familiar skin.
Ask again what they dream of.
Learn the new shape of their silence.

And if staying begins to mean
making yourself smaller each year,
remember that love is not a test
of how much of yourself you can lose.

The art is not staying at any cost.
It is choosing one another
without abandoning the self who chooses.
line: Lasting love needs two whole people, not one disappearing.

title: A Universe of My Own
body:
Eight billion stories, and I am one.
A line in a census,
a face blurred in a station,
a voice the night will soon forget.

Yet inside me, whole oceans move.
A childhood street can rise from one smell.
A single sentence can undo a year.
A stranger's kindness can change
the way tomorrow looks.

I am not the centre of everything.
I am not nothing.
I live in the strange middle,
small enough to be humbled,
large enough to be responsible
for what I do with this one life.
line: Humility and significance can coexist.

title: The Things We Carry
body:
We carry old conversations
like coins at the bottom of a pocket.
We carry the names of people
we no longer know how to call.

We carry the fear of repeating
what we promised ourselves would end.
We carry advice that once saved us
and now fits like someone else's coat.

Some things must be carried awhile.
Some things can be set down
at a bus stop, in a kitchen,
in the middle of a sentence.

I am learning to check my hands
before I blame the road for being heavy.
I am learning that letting go
is also a kind of strength.
line: You are allowed to outgrow what once protected you.

title: A Stranger in My Own Life
body:
I looked at my calendar
and could not remember choosing
half the things written there.

The days had become efficient.
The weeks had become indistinguishable.
I had learned to answer quickly
and rarely ask if I meant yes.

So I took a different street home.
Bought a pear from a man
who told me it was a good pear.
Sat on a wall and watched the buses.

Nothing dramatic happened.
But for a little while
I was not a passenger in my own life.
I was the one who chose the road.
line: Sometimes returning to yourself starts with one small choice.

title: The Kindness of Strangers
body:
A woman held the door
while I carried too many things.
A boy returned a glove
I had not noticed losing.
A tired cashier said, “Take your time,”
and meant it.

No orchestra followed.
No headline recorded the event.
The world did not become fair.

But something in me loosened.
I remembered that goodness
is not always a grand decision.
Sometimes it is a person
making a little room in the day
for someone they may never meet again.

I want to become that kind of ordinary.
line: Kindness is often small enough to be overlooked.

title: The Last Train
body:
The last train carries people
who have finished being somewhere
and have not yet arrived anywhere else.

A woman sleeps against the window.
A student watches the black glass
turn their face into a ghost.
Two friends share one earbud
and a joke that will not travel with them.

The stations arrive and disappear.
Nobody asks the night for a guarantee.
They step out when it is time,
carrying their separate weather.

I like the train for this:
it moves without knowing
what every passenger hopes to become.
line: We are all in transit more often than we admit.

title: Sunday Afternoon
body:
The afternoon stretches its legs.
A radio hums from another room.
The curtains move as if the house
is breathing in its sleep.

There is laundry to fold,
a message I can answer later,
a life I keep trying to turn
into a project with a deadline.

Today I let the hours remain unlabelled.
I eat toast over the sink.
I read the same paragraph twice.
I do not make a better version of myself.

By evening, nothing has been achieved.
Something has been lived.
line: A day does not need to be useful to be yours.

title: The Door That Opened
body:
I spent years pressing my ear
to a door that would not move.
I learned its grain by heart,
memorised the silence on the other side.

When I finally walked away,
I found another door standing open
at the end of the corridor.
It had been there all along,
though I could not see it
while I was facing the lock.

I do not call the years wasted.
They taught me what wanting can do
when it forgets to look around.

I am learning to turn the handle
without first asking permission from fear.
line: Not every closed door is a judgement of your worth.

title: The Lonely Crowd
body:
At the party, I knew everyone's name
and almost nobody's inner life.
We traded stories polished for company.
We laughed in the right places.
We left the difficult truths at home.

Later, the room emptied into taxis.
The music stopped pretending to hold us.
I stood by the sink with a glass
and felt the old distance return.

Maybe loneliness is not always being alone.
Maybe it is being present
without finding a place to put
the truest thing you came to say.
line: Being surrounded is not the same as being met.

title: The Sentence That Stayed
body:
I cannot remember the whole conversation.
I remember the rain on the pavement,
the paper cup going soft in my hand,
and one sentence you said without ceremony:
“You don't have to earn every breath.”

I carried it through a difficult month.
I set it beside the mirror.
I repeated it when rest felt undeserved
and kindness sounded like a language
I had never been taught.

You may have forgotten saying it.
I have not.
Some words do not change the world.
They change the room in which we meet it.
line: Never underestimate the sentence someone needs to hear.

title: The Blue Hour
body:
For a few minutes after sunset,
the world forgets its sharp edges.
The buildings turn blue.
Windows become small warm planets.
The birds make their last arguments
with the day.

I walk without headphones.
I let the street speak in its ordinary tongue:
a gate, a bicycle, a distant laugh.

The blue hour does not solve anything.
It only gives the unfinished day
a gentler way to end.

Sometimes that is enough
for a person to begin again tomorrow.
line: Gentleness can be a bridge between difficult days.

title: The Price of Being Understood
body:
I wanted to be understood
until understanding required explanation.
I wanted to be known
until someone noticed the contradiction.

I wanted a love that could read my mind
and a privacy nobody could enter.
I wanted to be chosen freely
and to control the choices that led there.

Human beings are full of unreasonable wishes.
We are not machines with clean instructions.
We are weather trying to describe itself
while changing shape.

Perhaps the work is not to become simple.
Perhaps it is to become honest
about the complicated thing we are.
line: Honesty is not simplicity; it is a willingness to be seen.

title: When the Music Ends
body:
We danced badly in a kitchen
with the windows open to the cold.
The song ended.
Neither of us moved to change it.

For a few seconds the room held
what the music had been carrying:
your hand, my shoulder,
the ordinary miracle of being here.

I think about that silence more
than the song itself.
Not because it lasted forever,
but because it did not have to.

Some moments are complete
without becoming permanent.
Some songs end
and leave the room full.
line: An ending does not erase the moment it held.

title: The Question Mark
body:
I used to think a question mark
was a hook meant to catch an answer.
Now I see it as a small figure
leaning forward in the dark.

It does not know what it will find.
It asks anyway.

Why this life?
Why this person?
Why does the heart keep making room
for things the mind has learned to fear?

Perhaps curiosity is not a road
that always leads somewhere.
Perhaps it is the way we stay awake
inside a world that cannot explain itself.

I put another question at the end.
The page looks more alive that way.
line: A good question can be a form of attention.

title: The Person I Am Becoming
body:
I am becoming someone
I would not have known how to describe
when I was younger.

Less certain, perhaps.
More careful with promises.
More willing to leave a room
where my laughter has to ask permission.

I have kept some old dreams.
I have buried others without a ceremony.
I have learned that changing direction
is not the same as betraying the destination.

If the younger me could see this life,
I hope they would recognise the courage,
not just the distance between the plan
and the person who made it here.
line: You can honour your past without living inside its plans.

title: The Smallest Planet
body:
There is a planet inside my chest
where the kettle is always warm,
where my oldest friend knows the door,
where a dog sleeps in a patch of sun.

It has no name in astronomy.
It will never appear in a textbook.
But it holds every place
where I have been allowed to exhale.

I used to search the universe
for proof that I mattered.
Now I build this small world carefully:
a meal, a promise kept,
a room where nobody has to pretend.

The stars are beautiful.
So is the life that happens beneath them.
line: Meaning can be built at human scale.

title: An Inventory of Hope
body:
One clean shirt.
A friend who answers honestly.
The plant that survived my neglect.
A song I have not ruined by overplaying.

A new route to the same familiar place.
The first cool evening after heat.
A book with a sentence waiting inside.
The fact that I am still curious.

Hope is not always a sunrise.
Sometimes it is a list made at a desk
by someone who cannot yet imagine
how the story gets better.

I write down what remains.
Not because it is enough forever,
but because it is enough to begin.
line: Hope can start as an inventory of what remains.

title: The Window Seat
body:
I choose the window seat
because watching the world pass
makes me feel both small and free.

A woman carries flowers through traffic.
A child waves at a bus.
A man stands in the rain
reading a message twice.

Every window frames a life
I will never fully know.
I used to find this lonely.
Today I find it astonishing.

The world is full of stories
that do not need me to witness them
for them to be real.
line: Other people's hidden lives are part of the wonder.

title: The Beautifully Unfinished
body:
There are sentences I have not finished,
roads I have not learned,
versions of myself still waiting
for the right season to arrive.

I used to hide the unfinished parts
as if they were evidence of failure.
Now I leave a little room around them.
A margin for the unexpected.
A place where a new thought can fit.

I am not a final edition.
I am a page with notes in the edges,
a story still listening for its next line.

If you find a mistake here,
please do not mistake it for the whole book.
line: You are allowed to be a work in progress.

title: The Last Word
body:
I wanted the last word
because I thought it might close the wound.
I rehearsed the perfect sentence
on walks, in showers, at red lights.

Then one day I forgot it.
A different life had begun to take up space.
The old argument shrank to its proper size:
a room I once lived in,
not the house I had to keep.

I never got the ending I imagined.
I got an afternoon without rehearsing,
a laugh that surprised me,
a silence that belonged to the present.

It turns out peace is not always
winning the conversation.
Sometimes it is leaving it behind.
line: You do not need the final word to move forward.
